### s3 (v0.12.0)

An S3 source and destination plugin for Conduit, written in Go.

The S3 connector is one of [Conduit](https://github.com/ConduitIO/conduit)
builtin plugins. It provides both, a source and a destination S3 connectors.

**Source**

The S3 Source Connector connects to a S3 bucket with the provided
configurations, using `aws.bucket`, `aws.accessKeyId`,`aws.secretAccessKey` and
`aws.region`. If the bucket doesn't exist, or the permissions fail, then an
error will occur. After that, the `Open` method is called to start the
connection from the provided position.

**Change Data Capture (CDC)**

This connector implements CDC features for S3 by scanning the bucket for changes
every `pollingPeriod` and detecting any change that happened after a certain
timestamp. These changes (update, delete, create) are then inserted into a
buffer that is checked on each Read request.

* To capture "delete" and "update", the S3 bucket versioning must be enabled.
* To capture "create" actions, the bucket versioning doesn't matter.

**Position Handling**

The connector goes through two modes.

* Snapshot mode: which loops through the S3 bucket and returns the objects that
  are already in there. The _Position_ during this mode is the object key
  attached to an underscore, an "s" for snapshot, and the _maxLastModifiedDate_
  found so far. As an example: "thisIsAKey_s12345", which makes the connector
  know at what mode it is and what object it last read. The
  _maxLastModifiedDate_ will be used when changing to CDC mode, the iterator
  will capture changes that happened after that.

* CDC mode: this mode iterates through the S3 bucket every `pollingPeriod` and
  captures new actions made on the bucket. the _Position_ during this mode is
  the object key attached to an underscore, a "c" for CDC, and the object's
  _lastModifiedDate_ in seconds. As an example: "thisIsAKey_c1634049397". This
  position is used to resume from the last record returned.

  **CDC mode is listing based and best effort, bounded by `lookbackPeriod`.**
  It detects changes by listing the bucket, which cannot be lossless: an
  object that becomes visible in a listing late can be missed. Lossless S3
  change capture needs bucket event notifications, which this connector does
  not use. Every poll selects the objects modified since `lookbackPeriod`
  (default 5m) before the newest object seen so far, and skips versions it
  already delivered, so objects that become visible late, within that
  window, are picked up: S3 stamps an object with the time its upload began,
  a multipart upload with the time it was initiated, and lists in key order.
  The object store's own timestamps decide, so the clock of the machine
  running Conduit does not matter, with one exception: the newest timestamp
  is capped at this machine's clock, so one bogus timestamp from the future
  (a store clock that stepped forward, or a misbehaving endpoint) cannot hide
  the objects written after it. The cap lowers the window's start, which
  causes redelivery. If this machine's clock is behind the store's by more
  than `lookbackPeriod` the source logs a warning with the code
  `s3.source.host_clock_behind_store`: the window is stretched by the skew.

  Delivery is at-least-once. After a restart the objects modified within
  `lookbackPeriod` of the newest object are delivered again. The snapshot
  hands over to CDC from the newest object that existed when the snapshot
  started (found by one extra listing of the prefix, one request per 1000
  keys, at the start of the snapshot), minus `lookbackPeriod`, so CDC
  redelivers the objects written while the snapshot ran, however long it
  took, plus those within `lookbackPeriod` before it started. On a bucket
  that was bulk loaded recently this can be every object of the load.

  The versions remembered for deduplication are limited to about 256 MiB
  (peak memory of a poll is about 1.5 times that, candidates included). If
  the objects inside the window need more, the window is **shortened**
  instead of stopping the source: the oldest remembered entries are
  forgotten by whole seconds and the window starts just above them. The
  source logs a warning with the code `s3.source.dedupe_window_shrunk`
  naming the effective lookback and the number of forgotten entries. While
  the window is shortened, an object that becomes visible late by more than
  the effective lookback can be missed, so the tolerance for late-visible
  objects is lower than `lookbackPeriod`; lower `lookbackPeriod` to avoid
  the shrinking. The source stops, with the error
  `s3.source.dedupe_window_overflow` (after a warning), only if the versions
  sharing a single second of `LastModified` do not fit, or when entries
  stamped at or after this machine's present second (a store clock that is
  ahead, or bogus timestamps from the future) take the budget: a shortened
  window never starts later than the present second, because that would hide
  the objects written from now on, so the source stops instead (the message
  names the clock skew and says to fix the clock). A store clock that is ahead
  by less than `lookbackPeriod` is normal and does not stop the source as long
  as the entries stamped in the present and the future fit the budget. A
  future-stamped object can therefore raise the start of the window at most
  up to the present second, never past it. The shortened window is not
  remembered across restarts: after a restart the window is rebuilt from the
  position and shortened again, so a restart delivers the window's objects
  again (duplicates, never a skip). When more objects share a second than
  one poll can hand over, they are delivered over several polls, oldest
  first, and the newest tracked entries may be dropped from tracking to make
  room; those are delivered again later (duplicates). A catch-up after
  downtime is delivered in bounded batches, oldest first. A resume position
  with a timestamp in the future, which only an older release could have
  written, is clamped to this machine's clock with a warning.

  Known limits (listing cannot see these, or sees them too late):
  * an upload that takes longer than `lookbackPeriod` to complete is missed
    when newer objects were seen in the meantime (multipart uploads carry
    their initiation time);
  * replica buckets whose replication lag exceeds `lookbackPeriod`;
  * a multipart upload that shares its initiation second with another object
    of the same key (a version already listed, or a second upload) is not
    tracked: it holds the settled cut instead (log code
    `s3.source.cut_held_same_second`, a warning every 15 minutes once the
    hold is older than that). New objects are delivered early until
    `cdc.maxEarlyObjects` is full and the rest wait, for as long as the
    upload runs, up to `cdc.maxPendingUploadAge`; after that the hold is
    released and the upload is tracked. Nothing is lost, only latency
    grows;
  * a multipart upload that is older than `cdc.maxPendingUploadAge` when
    the source first sees it, and shares its second with nothing, is not
    tracked (log code `s3.source.stale_upload_ignored`, error level): if it
    completes later its object can be missed. Abort such uploads, or add an
    AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload lifecycle rule with DaysAfterInitiation
    at most `cdc.maxPendingUploadAge`;
  * an identical re-put of an object within the same second is not seen as a
    change;
  * in an unversioned bucket an overwrite is reported as a create (there is
    no older version to compare with) and a delete is not reported;
  * in a versioned bucket intermediate versions that appear and are
    superseded within one poll are not emitted, only the latest; removing a
    delete marker (undelete) and permanently deleting the latest version are
    not emitted;
  * a GetObject that fails for another reason than the object having been
    deleted, for example an object archived to Glacier or Deep Archive,
    stops the source with that error.

  Objects deleted between being listed and being read are skipped, in the
  snapshot and in CDC. Values of `lookbackPeriod` above 1h log a warning and
  above 24h are rejected.

**Record Keys**

The S3 object key uniquely identifies the objects in an Amazon S3 bucket, which
is why a record key is the key read from the S3 bucket.

**Destination**

The S3 Destination Connector connects to an S3 bucket with the provided
configurations, using `aws.bucket`, `aws.accessKeyId`,`aws.secretAccessKey` and
`aws.region`. If the permissions fail, the connector will not be ready for
writing to S3.

**Writes and delivery**

Every batch the SDK hands to the destination (`sdk.batch.size` records, or
fewer after `sdk.batch.delay`; one record per batch by default) is written
with one `PutObject` per object, and the records are acknowledged only after
`PutObject` succeeded. Delivery is at-least-once: a batch that is retried
after a failure or a restart is written again as a new object, so a reader
can see a record twice, never zero times. Object names are
`<UnixNano>-<writer id>-<counter>.<ext>`: the write time in nanoseconds (so
objects still sort by write time), a random 16-hex-character id per
destination instance, and that instance's write counter. They are unique by
construction, also across pipelines or Conduit instances writing to the same
bucket and prefix in the same clock tick, and not deterministic (a retried
batch gets a new name). With `conditionalWrites` (default true) every
`PutObject` carries `If-None-Match: *`, so a store never replaces an existing
object. The records of a refused write are not acknowledged:

- `s3.destination.key_exists` (412): the key exists. Either another writer
  used it, or the AWS SDK retried this writer's own `PutObject` after the
  response to a successful first attempt was lost; in that case the records
  are already stored, and redelivering them writes a duplicate under a new
  key (at-least-once, nothing is lost).
- `s3.destination.conditional_conflict` (409): a conflicting operation on
  the key was in progress. Transient; a retry writes under a new key.
- `s3.destination.conditional_writes_unsupported`: the store rejects the
  header (501, or a 400/405 that names it). Set `conditionalWrites: false`;
  keys stay unique by construction.

A store that silently ignores `If-None-Match` writes unconditionally, with
no warning; the protection then rests on the unique names alone. Tested on
MinIO; AWS S3 documents support for conditional writes.

**Formats**

- `json`: one JSON object per line with `Operation`, `Position`, `Payload`,
  `Key` and `Metadata`; payload and key are JSON strings. A record whose key,
  payload, position or metadata is not valid UTF-8 is refused with the error
  `s3.destination.invalid_utf8` instead of being stored with replaced bytes.
- `parquet`: the same fields as string columns.
- `bytearray`: the payload bytes of every record, unchanged, each followed
  by `format.bytearray.separator` (default a newline). Structured payloads
  are written as their JSON encoding. A record without a payload (a delete,
  a Kafka tombstone) or with an empty one is refused with the error
  `s3.destination.null_value`; drop such records with a `filter` processor
  if they are expected. A Kafka tombstone arrives as an empty value, so an
  empty Kafka value cannot be told apart from it and is refused too. The
  separator is not escaped inside payloads: a payload that contains it
  cannot be split back unambiguously (as with Kafka Connect's
  `ByteArrayFormat`).

`compression` is `none` or `gzip` for `json` and `bytearray` (gzip appends
`.gz` to the extension and sets the content type to `application/gzip`), and
`none`, `gzip` (default) or `snappy` for `parquet`, where it is the column
codec.

When a record is refused, the records before it in the batch are written as
one object and acked, the refused record and the ones after it are nacked
(to the DLQ, if one is configured).

**Coming from the Kafka Connect S3 sink**

- `ByteArrayFormat` is `format: bytearray`; `format.bytearray.separator` and
  `format.bytearray.extension` have the same meaning (Kafka Connect's
  extension default is `.bin` as well).
- `JsonFormat` for topics with JSON values is `format: bytearray` with
  `format.bytearray.extension: .json`: the stored bytes are the record
  values. Kafka Connect re-serializes values through its converter, so
  whitespace and key order can differ, and `schemas.enable=true` envelopes
  are not produced.
- `s3.compression.type: gzip` is `compression: gzip`; `parquet.codec` is
  `compression` with `format: parquet` (Kafka Connect defaults to snappy,
  this connector to gzip).
- `behavior.on.null.values` other than `fail` has no counterpart.

**Server-side encryption**

By default the destination sends no server-side encryption header, so the
bucket's default encryption applies. On AWS every bucket encrypts new
objects with SSE-S3 unless it is configured otherwise, and a bucket whose
default is SSE-KMS gets SSE-KMS objects. An S3-compatible store without a
default encryption configuration stores objects unencrypted. When
`aws.serverSideEncryption` is empty, `Open` reads the bucket's default
encryption (`GetBucketEncryption`, permission
`s3:GetEncryptionConfiguration`) and logs a warning with the code
`s3.destination.bucket_unencrypted` if there is none. It never refuses to
start; without the permission the check is skipped (debug log).

Set `aws.serverSideEncryption` to `AES256`, `aws:kms` or `aws:kms:dsse` to
request a mode explicitly, and `aws.sseKmsKeyId` to pick the KMS key for the
two KMS modes. An explicit mode overrides the bucket default.

Upgrading from v0.9.5 or earlier: those versions sent `AES256` on every
write, whatever the bucket default was, so an SSE-KMS bucket default was
silently replaced by SSE-S3 (#1047). To keep the old behavior, set
`aws.serverSideEncryption: AES256`.

**Partitioning (Kafka Connect S3 sink layout)**

`partitioner` selects the directory layout under `prefix`:

| `partitioner` | Object key |
| --- | --- |
| `none` (default) | `<prefix>/<UnixNano>.<ext>` |
| `default` | `<prefix>/<collection>/partition=<kafka.partition>/<UnixNano>.<ext>` |
| `field` | `<prefix>/<collection>/<field>=<value>/.../<UnixNano>.<ext>` |
| `time`, `hourly`, `daily` | `<prefix>/<collection>/<time formatted with partitioner.pathFormat>/<UnixNano>.<ext>` |

`<collection>` is the `opencdc.collection` metadata, which `builtin:kafka`
sets to the topic, so with `prefix: topics` the directories are the ones the
Kafka Connect S3 sink writes, and tables or partition projections defined
over them keep working. `partitioner.pathFormat` takes Kafka Connect's
`path.format` syntax (numeric fields only), for example
`'year'=YYYY/'month'=MM/'day'=dd/'hour'=HH`. `hourly` and `daily` are Kafka
Connect's `HourlyPartitioner` and `DailyPartitioner`. Partition values are
escaped the way Hive escapes path names (`/` becomes `%2F`).

A batch is split into one object per directory. If one of those writes
fails, the records before the first record of the failed object are
acknowledged and the rest are nacked with the error: the pipeline stops,
or, with a dead-letter queue configured, those records go to it. Nothing is
acknowledged that is not stored. A restart delivers the nacked records
again, and records of objects that were already written can then be stored
twice (at-least-once). A record without the value its partitioner needs
(no collection, no `kafka.partition`, no `opencdc.createdAt`, a missing or
null field) is never written under an empty partition: it fails with the
error code `s3.destination.partition_value`.

Differences from Kafka Connect's `FieldPartitioner` that a reader of the
layout can notice:

- a null field fails the record (`s3.destination.partition_value`); Kafka
  Connect writes it under `field=null`;
- values are escaped as Hive escapes path names (`/` becomes `%2F`, `=`
  becomes `%3D`, and so on); Kafka Connect writes them unescaped, so a
  value with `/` there becomes extra directory levels;
- numbers keep the text they have in a raw JSON payload (`5`, `5.0`,
  `1e3` stay as written), and a number in structured data is written in its
  shortest form (`5` for 5.0). Kafka Connect writes the Java string of the
  converted value (`5.0` for a double, `1000.0` for `1e3`), so a double
  field with a whole value can land in `field=5` here and `field=5.0`
  there.

`builtin:kafka` does not set `kafka.partition` yet, so `partitioner: default`
needs it set by a processor until it does.

Author: Meroxa, Inc.

#### Source parameters

| Key | Type | Default | Required | Description | Validations |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aws.accessKeyId` | string |  | no | AWS access key id. Optional, but must be set together with aws.secretAccessKey. When both are unset the connector uses the Conduit host's ambient AWS identity (the AWS SDK default credential chain: environment, shared config and SSO, web identity/IRSA, ECS and EC2 roles), but only if the Conduit operator enabled connectors.ambient-credentials and listed the bucket, and only as the built-in connector (builtin:s3). Otherwise the connector refuses with connector.ambient_credentials_disabled. |  |
| `aws.bucket` | string |  | yes | the AWS S3 bucket name. | required |
| `aws.endpoint` | string |  | no | The endpoint to connect to. Set this when using an S3-compatible object store such as MinIO (for example http://localhost:9000). Leave empty to use the default AWS endpoints. The AWS_ENDPOINT_URL environment variable is also honored when this is empty. Note that an http:// endpoint sends every request, including the SigV4 Authorization header that carries the access key ID, in the clear: use https:// for anything that is not on localhost. |  |
| `aws.pathStyle` | bool | false | no | Use path-style addressing (http://endpoint/bucket/key) instead of virtual-hosted addressing (http://bucket.endpoint/key). Set this to true when using an S3-compatible store that does not support virtual-hosted addressing. The default MinIO setup (started without MINIO_DOMAIN) is one: it ignores the bucket in the host name and takes the first path segment as the bucket instead. What comes back depends on the key: with a prefix configured the remaining segments are still a key, so PutObject fails with a 404 NoSuchBucket; without a prefix there is no key left and MinIO answers with a 400 MalformedXML. Leave false for AWS S3. |  |
| `aws.region` | string |  | yes | the AWS S3 bucket region | required |
| `aws.secretAccessKey` | string |  | no | AWS secret access key. Optional, but must be set together with aws.accessKeyId. See aws.accessKeyId for ambient credentials. |  |
| `cdc.maxEarlyObjects` | int | 16384 | no | The largest number of new objects delivered before they settle (the early set kept in every position, about 20 bytes per object). A bucket written faster than cdc.maxEarlyObjects / lookbackPeriod gets the excess up to lookbackPeriod later. Memory: positions take up to records in flight x (80 + key length + 20 x this) bytes. 0 delivers everything only once settled. At most 16384. The default delivers a burst of the SDK acceptance suite's maximum batch (10000) at once instead of deferring it for lookbackPeriod. |  |
| `cdc.maxPendingUploadAge` | duration | 24h | no | Multipart uploads initiated longer ago than this are not tracked (an abandoned upload would otherwise occupy a slot forever); if one still completes, its object can be missed. Add an AbortIncompleteMultipartUpload lifecycle rule with DaysAfterInitiation at most this. Must be at least lookbackPeriod. |  |
| `cdc.maxSettledBytesPerPoll` | int | 67108864 | no | The memory budget, in bytes, for the settled objects one poll delivers (a catch-up after downtime continues on the next poll). |  |
| `cdc.maxTrackedUploads` | int | 256 | no | The largest number of long-running multipart uploads tracked in a position. When more run at once, the oldest untracked one delays settling until a slot frees up. At most 10000. |  |
| `cdc.multipartHold` | bool | true | no | Track in-progress multipart uploads, so that an upload running longer than lookbackPeriod is not missed (AWS stamps the completed object with the time the upload started). Needs s3:ListBucketMultipartUploads. false skips it and is lossy for such uploads. |  |
| `lookbackPeriod` | duration | 5m | no | The late-visibility tolerance of change capture. An object is "settled" once it is older than this (by the store's clock); the source assumes that no object becomes visible in listings later than this after its LastModified (replication lag, a slow PUT and clock skew between store nodes must stay below it; multipart uploads are tracked separately). New objects are delivered at once while they fit cdc.maxEarlyObjects, the rest when they settle, so this is also the maximum extra latency on a busy bucket. Positions resume exactly whatever the value. 30s or more is supported; 1s to 29s is deprecated (a warning; rejected in a later release); 0 is accepted but lossy for late-visible objects; above 24h is rejected. |  |
| `pollingPeriod` | duration | 1s | no | polling period for the CDC mode, formatted as a time.Duration string. |  |
| `prefix` | string |  | no | the S3 key prefix. |  |
| `sdk.batch.delay` | duration | 0 | no | Maximum delay before an incomplete batch is read from the source. |  |
| `sdk.batch.size` | int | 0 | no | Maximum size of batch before it gets read from the source. | greater-than(-1) |
| `sdk.schema.context.enabled` | bool | true | no | Specifies whether to use a schema context name. If set to false, no schema context name will be used, and schemas will be saved with the subject name specified in the connector (not safe because of name conflicts). |  |
| `sdk.schema.context.name` | string |  | no | Schema context name to be used. Used as a prefix for all schema subject names. If empty, defaults to the connector ID. |  |
| `sdk.schema.extract.key.enabled` | bool | false | no | Whether to extract and encode the record key with a schema. |  |
| `sdk.schema.extract.key.subject` | string | key | no | The subject of the key schema. If the record metadata contains the field "opencdc.collection" it is prepended to the subject name and separated with a dot. |  |
| `sdk.schema.extract.payload.enabled` | bool | false | no | Whether to extract and encode the record payload with a schema. |  |
| `sdk.schema.extract.payload.subject` | string | payload | no | The subject of the payload schema. If the record metadata contains the field "opencdc.collection" it is prepended to the subject name and separated with a dot. |  |
| `sdk.schema.extract.type` | string | avro | no | The type of the payload schema. | inclusion(avro) |

#### Destination parameters

| Key | Type | Default | Required | Description | Validations |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `aws.accessKeyId` | string |  | no | AWS access key id. Optional, but must be set together with aws.secretAccessKey. When both are unset the connector uses the Conduit host's ambient AWS identity (the AWS SDK default credential chain: environment, shared config and SSO, web identity/IRSA, ECS and EC2 roles), but only if the Conduit operator enabled connectors.ambient-credentials and listed the bucket, and only as the built-in connector (builtin:s3). Otherwise the connector refuses with connector.ambient_credentials_disabled. |  |
| `aws.bucket` | string |  | yes | the AWS S3 bucket name. | required |
| `aws.endpoint` | string |  | no | The endpoint to connect to. Set this when using an S3-compatible object store such as MinIO (for example http://localhost:9000). Leave empty to use the default AWS endpoints. The AWS_ENDPOINT_URL environment variable is also honored when this is empty. Note that an http:// endpoint sends every request, including the SigV4 Authorization header that carries the access key ID, in the clear: use https:// for anything that is not on localhost. |  |
| `aws.pathStyle` | bool | false | no | Use path-style addressing (http://endpoint/bucket/key) instead of virtual-hosted addressing (http://bucket.endpoint/key). Set this to true when using an S3-compatible store that does not support virtual-hosted addressing. The default MinIO setup (started without MINIO_DOMAIN) is one: it ignores the bucket in the host name and takes the first path segment as the bucket instead. What comes back depends on the key: with a prefix configured the remaining segments are still a key, so PutObject fails with a 404 NoSuchBucket; without a prefix there is no key left and MinIO answers with a 400 MalformedXML. Leave false for AWS S3. |  |
| `aws.region` | string |  | yes | the AWS S3 bucket region | required |
| `aws.secretAccessKey` | string |  | no | AWS secret access key. Optional, but must be set together with aws.accessKeyId. See aws.accessKeyId for ambient credentials. |  |
| `aws.serverSideEncryption` | string |  | no | Server-side encryption to request for every object written: AES256 (SSE-S3), aws:kms (SSE-KMS) or aws:kms:dsse (DSSE-KMS). Leave empty to send no encryption header, so the bucket's default encryption applies (on AWS every bucket encrypts with SSE-S3 by default; an S3-compatible store may store the object unencrypted). An explicit value overrides the bucket default: setting AES256 on a bucket whose default is SSE-KMS stores objects with SSE-S3 instead. |  |
| `aws.sseKmsKeyId` | string |  | no | The KMS key ID, key ARN, alias name or alias ARN to encrypt objects with. Only valid when aws.serverSideEncryption is aws:kms or aws:kms:dsse; when empty with those modes, S3 uses the bucket's default KMS key, or the AWS managed key aws/s3. |  |
| `compression` | string |  | no | Compression of the objects: none or gzip for json and bytearray (gzip appends .gz to the extension), none, gzip or snappy (the column codec) for parquet. Empty means the format's default: none for json and bytearray, gzip for parquet. |  |
| `conditionalWrites` | bool | true | no | Send If-None-Match: * with every PutObject, so that the store refuses to replace an existing object (error s3.destination.key_exists) instead of silently overwriting one whose records were already acknowledged. Object keys are unique by construction; this makes any collision fail loudly (a 412 can also be the AWS SDK retrying this writer's own write after a lost response: then the redelivered records are a duplicate, never a loss). Tested on MinIO; AWS S3 documents support. Set to false for a store that answers with s3.destination.conditional_writes_unsupported. A store that silently ignores the header writes unconditionally, without a warning. |  |
| `format` | string |  | yes | The destination format: "json" (one OpenCDC-shaped JSON object per line), "parquet", or "bytearray" (the payload bytes of every record followed by format.bytearray.separator; Kafka Connect's ByteArrayFormat, and with format.bytearray.extension set to .json the bytes Kafka Connect's JsonFormat writes for JSON values). bytearray fails a record without a payload (a delete or a Kafka tombstone) or with an empty one (indistinguishable from a tombstone) with the error s3.destination.null_value; json fails a record that is not valid UTF-8 with s3.destination.invalid_utf8. | required, inclusion(parquet,json,bytearray) |
| `format.bytearray.extension` | string | .bin | no | File extension of objects written by format bytearray, with or without the leading dot. |  |
| `format.bytearray.separator` | string | \n | no | Written after every record by format bytearray. The escapes \n, \r, \t and \\ are resolved. The separator is not escaped inside payloads, so a payload that contains it cannot be split back unambiguously (as with Kafka Connect's ByteArrayFormat); pick a separator the data cannot contain, or use json or parquet. |  |
| `partitioner` | string | none | no | The directory layout under the prefix (<name> is the object name, <UnixNano>-<writer id>-<counter>). "none" writes every batch to <prefix>/<name>.<ext>, as earlier versions do. The others reproduce the directories of the Kafka Connect S3 sink's partitioners, under <prefix>/<collection>/ (the collection is the opencdc.collection metadata, the topic for records from builtin:kafka): "default" adds partition=<kafka.partition metadata>, "field" adds <field>=<value> per field in partitioner.fields, "time" adds the record time formatted with partitioner.pathFormat, "hourly" and "daily" are "time" with Kafka Connect's hourly and daily patterns. A batch is split into one object per directory. A record that lacks the value its partitioner needs is not written: it fails with the error code s3.destination.partition_value. | inclusion(none,default,field,time,hourly,daily) |
| `partitioner.duration` | duration |  | no | The width of a time partition for partitioner "time", at least 1s (Kafka Connect: partition.duration.ms). The record time is floored to a multiple of it in partitioner.timezone. |  |
| `partitioner.fields` | string |  | no | Comma-separated payload fields for partitioner "field", dots for nested fields (Kafka Connect: partition.field.name). The payload must be structured data or a raw JSON object. |  |
| `partitioner.pathFormat` | string |  | no | The directory pattern for partitioner "time", in Kafka Connect's path.format syntax: yyyy or YYYY, MM, dd, HH, mm, ss, and quoted literal text, for example 'year'=YYYY/'month'=MM/'day'=dd/'hour'=HH. Text fields (MMM) are not supported. |  |
| `partitioner.timestampExtractor` | string | record | no | Where the time partitioners take the time from: "record" (the opencdc.createdAt metadata, the Kafka record timestamp for builtin:kafka), "recordField" (the payload field in partitioner.timestampField: epoch milliseconds, an RFC 3339 string or a time) or "wallclock" (the time of the write; a redelivered record can land in a later directory). | inclusion(record,recordField,wallclock) |
| `partitioner.timestampField` | string |  | no | The payload field for timestampExtractor "recordField", dots for nested fields (Kafka Connect: timestamp.field). |  |
| `partitioner.timezone` | string | UTC | no | The IANA time zone the time partitioners floor and format in. |  |
| `prefix` | string |  | no | the S3 key prefix. |  |
| `sdk.batch.delay` | duration | 1s | no | Maximum delay before an incomplete batch is written to the destination. |  |
| `sdk.batch.size` | int | 1000 | no | Maximum size of batch before it gets written to the destination. | greater-than(-1) |
| `sdk.rate.burst` | int | 0 | no | Allow bursts of at most X records (0 or less means that bursts are not limited). Only takes effect if a rate limit per second is set. Note that if `sdk.batch.size` is bigger than `sdk.rate.burst`, the effective batch size will be equal to `sdk.rate.burst`. | greater-than(-1) |
| `sdk.rate.perSecond` | float | 0 | no | Maximum number of records written per second (0 means no rate limit). | greater-than(-1) |
| `sdk.record.format` | string | opencdc/json | no | The format of the output record. See the Conduit documentation for a full list of supported formats (https://conduitdata.io/docs/using/connectors/configuration-parameters/output-format). |  |
| `sdk.record.format.options` | string |  | no | Options to configure the chosen output record format. Options are normally key=value pairs separated with comma (e.g. opt1=val2,opt2=val2), except for the `template` record format, where options are a Go template. |  |
| `sdk.schema.extract.key.enabled` | bool | true | no | Whether to extract and decode the record key with a schema. |  |
| `sdk.schema.extract.payload.enabled` | bool | true | no | Whether to extract and decode the record payload with a schema. |  |

## 3. Error codes (187)

| Reason | gRPC status | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `api.content_type_unsupported` | InvalidArgument | CodeContentTypeUnsupported is returned by the HTTP API when a mutating request (POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE) with a body does not use Content-Type: application/json. |
| `api.host_forbidden` | PermissionDenied | CodeHostForbidden is returned by the HTTP API on a loopback bind when the Host header is not localhost, 127.0.0.1, [::1] or a configured allowed host (DNS rebinding protection). |
| `api.origin_forbidden` | PermissionDenied | CodeOriginForbidden is returned by the HTTP API when a request's Origin header is neither allowlisted nor same-origin. |
| `api.token_invalid` | InvalidArgument | CodeTokenInvalid is raised at startup when the configured API token is unusable: the token file cannot be read, the token is empty or too short, or both api.token and api.token-file are set. |
| `api.token_required` | FailedPrecondition | CodeTokenRequired is raised at startup when the HTTP or gRPC API is bound to a non-loopback address and no API token is configured. Conduit refuses to serve an unauthenticated API to the network. |
| `api.unauthenticated` | Unauthenticated | CodeUnauthenticated is returned by the HTTP and gRPC APIs when a request carries no bearer token or the wrong one. |
| `cli.invalid_usage` | InvalidArgument | CodeInvalidUsage is raised when a command is invoked wrongly, before it does any work: an unknown or malformed flag, a missing or extra positional argument, a required flag left out, or flag values that fail to parse. It is distinct from common.invalid_argument because the fix is always to change the command line (see the command's --help), not the input it reads. InvalidArgument puts it in the validation exit bucket (exit 2, pkg/conduit/exitcode). |
| `common.invalid_argument` | InvalidArgument | CodeInvalidArgument is a generic invalid-input error. |
| `common.not_found` | NotFound | CodeNotFound is a generic not-found error. |
| `common.unavailable` | Unavailable | CodeUnavailable is raised when Conduit itself cannot reach a required external dependency it needs to start or operate: the CLI can't reach a running server, the configured database can't be opened/dialed, or a listen address is already bound. It is deliberately generic (unlike the per-domain codes elsewhere in the registry) because these are environment-of-execution failures, not domain business errors — the caller's remediation is "check the environment", not "fix a config field".  It maps to the gRPC Unavailable category, which pkg/conduit/exitcode's classifier treats as an environment failure (process exit code 3), distinct from validation errors (exit 2) and internal/runtime errors (exit 1). |
| `config.ambient_proxy_env` | FailedPrecondition | CodeAmbientProxyEnv is a startup error: ambient credentials are enabled while an HTTP proxy variable is set and allow-proxy is false. |
| `config.ambient_resource_wildcard` | InvalidArgument | CodeAmbientResourceWildcard is a startup error: an entry of connectors.ambient-credentials.allow-resources contains '*'. Bucket names are globally registrable, so a pattern would admit buckets anyone can create. |
| `config.env_ref_malformed` | InvalidArgument | CodeEnvRefMalformed is raised when a setting contains a "$" reference that is not a plain ${NAME} or $NAME (defaults such as ${NAME:-x}, nested references, an unterminated "${", or "$" followed by a digit or a shell special such as $1 and $*). Write the plain form, or use $$ for a literal dollar sign. A "$" at the end of a value or before a space or punctuation is a literal dollar sign and is not an error. |
| `config.env_var_missing` | InvalidArgument | CodeEnvVarMissing is raised when a ${VAR} reference cannot be resolved because the environment variable is not set. The fix is to set the variable and restart the pipeline. |
| `config.env_var_not_allowed` | PermissionDenied | CodeEnvVarNotAllowed is raised when a setting references an environment variable that is not in the operator's env.allow list. The fix is for the operator to add the name to env.allow in conduit.yaml (or pass --env.allow) and restart; it cannot be changed through the API. |
| `config.field_invalid` | InvalidArgument | config: field invalid |
| `config.field_renamed` | InvalidArgument | CodeFieldRenamed is the stable code carried by a lint warning for a deprecated field that was mechanically renamed (the old key's value moves unchanged to a new key) — see pkg/provisioning/config/yaml/internal.Change.RenamedTo and (*configLinter).newWarning. It is distinct from the generic validate.CodeLintWarning so cmd/conduit/internal/repair's fix-producer scan (design doc 20260712-repair-command.md §6, item #1) can find exactly these findings without pattern-matching warning text. |
| `config.field_required` | InvalidArgument | config: field required |
| `config.field_too_long` | InvalidArgument | config: field too long |
| `config.id_duplicate` | InvalidArgument | config: id duplicate |
| `config.parse_error` | InvalidArgument | CodeParseError is raised when a pipeline config document can't be parsed at all (invalid YAML, unrecognized version). It exists for offline consumers (cmd/conduit/internal/validate) that need a stable code for parser failures, which the parser itself returns as plain errors since it has no per-field configPath to attach at that stage. |
| `config.path_not_allowed` | PermissionDenied | CodePathNotAllowed is raised when a path in a setting is outside every directory the operator allows for it (or no directory is allowed). The fix is for an operator to allow the directory in conduit.yaml and restart; it cannot be changed through the API. |
| `connector.ambient_credentials_disabled` | PermissionDenied | CodeAmbientCredentialsDisabled is raised when a built-in connector has no static credentials and the operator has not enabled ambient credentials. |
| `connector.credentials_incomplete` | PermissionDenied | CodeCredentialsIncomplete is raised when only one of a static credential pair is set; it never falls back to ambient credentials. |
| `connector.delete_hook_ran` | FailedPrecondition | CodeConnectorDeleteHookRan is raised when a connector is started after a delete that was rolled back but had already delivered the "deleted" lifecycle event to the plugin. The plugin may have released resources its saved position depends on (for example a Postgres replication slot), so resuming from that position could skip records. The connector refuses to start until it is deleted and created again, or Conduit is restarted after the resources were checked (#3137). |
| `connector.delete_hook_unresolvable` | FailedPrecondition | CodeConnectorDeleteHookUnresolvable is raised when a connector is deleted while its stored settings no longer resolve (an environment variable that left env.allow or is gone, a path outside the allowed directories), so the plugin's "deleted" hook cannot run. Deleting anyway would leave what the hook cleans up behind: a Postgres replication slot keeps retaining WAL on the database until someone drops it. The delete is refused; restore the setting, or delete with force to skip the hook. |
| `connector.egress_blocked` | PermissionDenied | CodeEgressBlocked is raised when a connector setting names a target that is not allowed. It cannot be changed through the API: a metadata endpoint is never allowed, and the allowlist is the operator's. |
| `connector.endpoint_link_local` | PermissionDenied | CodeEndpointLinkLocal is raised when an ambient-credential connection would go to a link-local or cloud metadata address. |
| `connector.endpoint_not_allowed` | PermissionDenied | CodeEndpointNotAllowed is raised when, under ambient credentials, an endpoint is not https or not an exact allow-endpoints entry. |
| `connector.external_unreachable` | Unavailable | CodeExternalConnectorUnreachable is raised when an external connector's dialed address (pkg/plugin/connector/external, embed Slice 2) cannot be reached - at registration time (fail fast, never discovered on the first pipeline record) or when the connection is lost. |
| `connector.external_version_mismatch` | FailedPrecondition | CodeExternalConnectorVersionMismatch is raised when an external connector's dialed address does not implement the pconnector protocol version pkg/plugin/connector/external's Dispenser hard-coded (go-plugin performs no version negotiation on the Reattach path, so this package must verify it explicitly via a Specify round trip). |
| `connector.instance_not_found` | NotFound | CodeConnectorNotFound is raised when a referenced connector instance cannot be located. |
| `connector.invalid_type` | InvalidArgument | CodeConnectorInvalidType is raised when a connector type is neither "source" nor "destination". |
| `connector.plugin_not_found` | NotFound | CodeConnectorPluginNotFound is raised when a referenced connector plugin cannot be located. |
| `connector.proxy_not_allowed` | PermissionDenied | CodeProxyNotAllowed is raised when a proxy variable is set and the operator has not set connectors.ambient-credentials.allow-proxy. |
| `connector.redirect_refused` | PermissionDenied | CodeRedirectRefused is raised when a server redirects an ambient-credential request to another host or a non-https URL. |
| `connector.resource_not_allowed` | PermissionDenied | CodeResourceNotAllowed is raised when a resource (an S3 bucket) is not an exact allow-resources entry, or is an ARN or alias form. |
| `connector.running` | FailedPrecondition | CodeConnectorRunning is raised when an operation requires the connector to not be running, but a connector instance for it already exists. |
| `connector.standalone_not_allowlisted` | PermissionDenied | CodeStandaloneNotAllowlisted is raised when a pipeline references a standalone connector while connectors.egress.allow is set. Standalone connectors are separate processes that never receive the engine's dialer, so the allowlist cannot bind them; they are refused at dispatch (fail closed) rather than run unconstrained. |
| `connector.state_persist_failed` | Unavailable | CodeConnectorStatePersistFailed is raised when a connector's state write (source position, last active config) could not be committed to the store. When one connector's write fails, only that connector receives this error and the rest of the batch is committed. When opening or committing the transaction fails, every connector still in that attempt receives it. A source that receives it has not acked the affected positions upstream, so a restart re-reads from the last stored position. |
| `debezium.avro_unsupported` | Unimplemented | CodeAvroUnsupported is raised when key.converter or value.converter is "avro": the Confluent AvroConverter (AvroData port, subject naming, Confluent wire format) is not implemented yet. It fails at configure time, before any record is encoded, so a misconfigured pipeline never emits a half-encoded message. |
| `debezium.config_invalid` | InvalidArgument | CodeConfigInvalid is raised when the processor settings are invalid. |
| `debezium.descriptor_missing` | FailedPrecondition | CodeDescriptorMissing is raised when a record carries no debezium.descriptor, or a descriptor that does not match this format.version. |
| `debezium.old_key_unavailable` | InvalidArgument | CodeOldKeyUnavailable is raised on a primary-key change whose debezium.old_key is missing or unparsable, so the delete and tombstone cannot be keyed. |
| `debezium.record_schema_mismatch` | InvalidArgument | CodeRecordSchemaMismatch is raised when a record's key, before or after does not match the descriptor: a missing required field, an unknown field, or a value of the wrong type. It never coerces (invariant 6). |
| `debezium.unsupported_type` | InvalidArgument | CodeUnsupportedType is raised when a descriptor names a Connect type this encoder cannot serialize. |
| `debezium.value_out_of_range` | InvalidArgument | CodeValueOutOfRange is raised when a value does not fit its declared schema (a decimal wider than its scale, a timestamp outside the epoch microsecond range). |
| `generate.ambiguous_prompt` | InvalidArgument | CodeAmbiguousPrompt: the request could not be pinned to a pipeline.  Raised in two places, deliberately conservative pre-call (design §9): before any provider call ONLY when the prompt is empty or names one role for two different connectors; otherwise post-hoc, when a candidate's connectors cannot be traced to anything the request actually said. A merely terse request is never refused pre-call — it goes to the model, which reads intent far better than a keyword table, and the result is judged the normal way. |
| `generate.ambiguous_provider_configuration` | InvalidArgument | CodeAmbiguousProvider: more than one candidate and no explicit choice. This is an error rather than a pick — see the package doc. |
| `generate.destination_exists` | AlreadyExists | CodeDestinationExists: the resolved output path already exists and --force was not passed (design §8, amended 2026-08-21).  It is a code of its own rather than the foundational common.invalid_argument because the consumer is frequently an agent, and "that file already exists" is fixed by re-running with --force or a different --out, while a generic invalid-argument is fixed by changing the request. A caller that cannot tell those apart from the code has to parse the message.  AlreadyExists shares the Validation exit bucket with InvalidArgument (pkg/conduit/exitcode, fromGRPCCode), so this is additive: the process still exits 2, only the reason string a machine reads gets more specific. |
| `generate.no_provider_configured` | Unauthenticated | CodeNoProviderConfigured: zero resolvable candidates. Unauthenticated (exit 3, environment) rather than InvalidArgument, because the user's command was fine — their environment is not. |
| `generate.parse_failed` | Internal | CodeParseFailed: the provider replied, but nothing in the reply could be read as a pipeline config within the retry budget. Internal (exit 1, runtime) rather than InvalidArgument, because the user's request was well-formed — the boundary failed, not their input. |
| `generate.provider_error` | Unavailable | CodeProviderError covers every way the provider call itself failed: network, timeout, rate limit, or an auth rejection from the provider. Unavailable (exit 3, environment) because the user's command was fine. |
| `generate.semantic_mismatch` | FailedPrecondition | CodeSemanticMismatch: the candidate passed validate but did not do what was asked — wrong connector, swapped direction, a requested filter missing. A schema-valid pipeline that confidently does the wrong thing is the failure mode the semantic checker exists for, so it gets its own code rather than hiding inside validate_failed. |
| `generate.validate_failed` | FailedPrecondition | CodeValidateFailed: a candidate parsed but never passed validate within the retry budget. FailedPrecondition (exit 2, validation): the request was understood, the artifact it produced is not usable as-is, and the findings say exactly why.  The last attempt's validate.Report travels back on Result.Report — it is never discarded, because the findings are the only thing that tells the user (or an agent) what to change. |
| `internal.error` | Internal | CodeInternal is a coded internal failure. |
| `internal.unknown` | Internal | CodeUnknown is the fallback when an un-coded error reaches a boundary. |
| `kc.connector_class_unsupported` | InvalidArgument | CodeConnectorClassUnsupported: the connector class has no mapping; every key of the connector is listed with this code and no pipeline is written. |
| `kc.consumer_group_shared` | InvalidArgument | CodeConsumerGroupShared: a connector-level note that a migrated sink's Kafka source reads in the consumer group the Kafka Connect sink commits its offsets to, so the Kafka Connect connector must be stopped before the pipeline starts. Not blocking: two live consumers in one group split the partitions between them, which delays records and duplicates none, and the operator is the only one who can stop it. |
| `kc.converter_unknown` | InvalidArgument | CodeConverterUnknown: a connector-level note when neither the connector nor the worker file sets key.converter or value.converter, so the wire format is unknown. Blocking. |
| `kc.converter_unsupported` | InvalidArgument | CodeConverterUnsupported: a converter with no Conduit equivalent in this version. Blocking: the wire format would differ. |
| `kc.default_differs` | InvalidArgument | CodeDefaultDiffers: a connector-level note for an absent key whose Kafka Connect default differs from Conduit's behavior. |
| `kc.delivery_semantics_differ` | InvalidArgument | CodeDeliverySemanticsDiffer: a connector-level note that a Kafka Connect delivery guarantee is not reproduced, for example the S3 sink's deterministic object names, which give exactly-once object keys. |
| `kc.key_approximated` | InvalidArgument | CodeKeyApproximated: translated with a documented difference. |
| `kc.key_conflict` | InvalidArgument | CodeKeyConflict: two keys map onto one Conduit setting. Blocking, since either value could be the one Kafka Connect used. |
| `kc.key_deprecated` | InvalidArgument | CodeKeyDeprecated: a legacy key name, handled as its current name. |
| `kc.key_duplicate` | InvalidArgument | CodeKeyDuplicate: an earlier occurrence of a key that appears again later in the same connector config; the last value wins. |
| `kc.key_required` | InvalidArgument | CodeKeyRequired: a connector-level note for a key the upstream connector requires (it has no default) that the config does not set. Kafka Connect rejects such a config. Blocking. |
| `kc.key_unknown` | InvalidArgument | CodeKeyUnknown: no rule claims the key. Always blocking: an unknown key may change behavior, and the safe direction is to stop. |
| `kc.key_unsupported` | InvalidArgument | CodeKeyUnsupported: a known key with no Conduit equivalent for its value. |
| `kc.offsets_not_migrated` | InvalidArgument | CodeOffsetsNotMigrated: a connector-level note that the connector resumes from offsets Kafka Connect stored, which migrate does not carry over; the note says where the pipeline starts instead. Blocking: records are copied again or skipped. |
| `kc.output_shape_differs` | InvalidArgument | CodeOutputShapeDiffers: a connector-level note that records, objects or topics differ in shape or layout from the original connector's. |
| `kc.resume_unavailable` | InvalidArgument | CodeResumeUnavailable: a key needs the Debezium offset import (or another cutover mechanism) to resume where the original connector stopped, and that mechanism was not requested or is not available. Blocking: starting fresh would skip or replay records. |
| `kc.secret_plaintext` | InvalidArgument | CodeSecretPlaintext: a connector-level note that the input holds a secret as a literal value. The value is not copied anywhere, but the input file is itself a leak. |
| `kc.setting_required` | InvalidArgument | CodeSettingRequired: a connector-level note for a setting the Conduit plugin requires that no Kafka Connect key provides; it is written as an environment variable to fill. Blocking: the pipeline cannot run as is. |
| `kc.smt_unsupported` | InvalidArgument | CodeSMTUnsupported: a single message transform or predicate outside the subset migrate translates exactly. Blocking: transforms change data. |
| `kc.target_capability_missing` | InvalidArgument | CodeTargetCapabilityMissing: a key maps to a Conduit setting the target plugin does not provide yet (a requires-gate param or capability the connector lane has not shipped). Blocking: writing nothing would drop the setting, so the migration stops until the lane lands. |
| `kc.topic_name_unsupported` | InvalidArgument | CodeTopicNameUnsupported: a connector-level note that the connector's topic naming cannot be written as the destination's topic template. Blocking: the destination topic must be set by hand. |
| `lifecycle_v2.partial_graceful_stop_escalated` | Aborted | CodePartialGracefulStopEscalated is returned by Stop/StopAndWait for an N-source pipeline (slice 3b of the arch-v2 multi-connector epic) when a graceful stop arms some sources within the deadline but not others. See stopRunnablePipeline's doc and the adversarial-review finding this closes (H1, docs/design-documents/20260801-archv2-multiconnector-nsource.md).  Leaving that state unresolved would strand the pipeline reporting StatusRunning indefinitely: the still-unarmed worker(s) keep reading, workersWg never drains, and runPipeline's cleanup goroutine (the only thing that ever writes a terminal status) never runs - invisible to an operator except as an error return that may go to a disconnected caller. Instead the pipeline's tomb is force-killed with this code so every still-unarmed worker's next context check observes cancellation and unwinds, guaranteeing the pipeline reaches a terminal (Degraded) status instead of a silent, half-stopped one. At-least-once is preserved: this never acks anything, so an interrupted worker's in-flight, unacked batch simply replays on the pipeline's next start (invariant 3). |
| `lifecycle_v2.stop_and_wait_timeout` | DeadlineExceeded | lifecycle v2: stop and wait timeout |
| `migrate.connector_name_invalid` | InvalidArgument | CodeConnectorNameInvalid is raised when a connector has no name, or two connectors of one run share a name. Each connector becomes one pipeline named after it, so either case would leave a pipeline unnamed or written over another. |
| `migrate.input_too_large` | InvalidArgument | CodeInputTooLarge is raised when the inputs exceed [MaxInputBytes] in total, [MaxInputs] in number, or [MaxJSONDepth] in JSON nesting. |

| `orchestrator.redacted_setting_plugin_changed` | InvalidArgument | CodeRedactedSettingPluginChanged is raised when an update sends "***" for a setting while changing the plugin (including only its version). A stored value, typically a credential, is never carried to a different plugin; the update must send real values. |
| `orchestrator.redacted_setting_with_other_changes` | InvalidArgument | CodeRedactedSettingWithOtherChanges is raised when an update sends "***" (keep the stored value) for a setting while any other setting in the same update changes: a different value, an added key, or a removed key. A stored value is kept only by a pure round trip, so an update that repoints a host or URL cannot also ask Conduit to send the stored credential there. The update must send real values. |
| `orchestrator.redacted_setting_without_stored_value` | InvalidArgument | CodeRedactedSettingWithoutStoredValue is raised when an update sends the redacted placeholder "***" for a setting that has no stored value. "***" in an update means "keep the stored value"; with nothing stored there is nothing to keep, and storing "***" itself would silently break the setting. |
| `pipeline.archv2_destination_batching_unsupported` | FailedPrecondition | CodeArchV2DestinationBatchingUnsupported is returned by Start, and by the live-apply preflight (PreflightPipelineConfig), when a pipeline would run on the preview pipeline architecture v2 (--preview.pipeline-arch-v2) and the dead-letter-queue connector sets sdk.batch.size above 1 (#2979).  Regular destinations are no longer refused by this code: the funnel now batches destination writes itself using the destination's sdk.batch.size/sdk.batch.delay (see docs/design-documents/20261017-funnel-destination-batching.md) and strips the settings from the SDK plugin, so a destination batch can no longer withhold its acks and stall the stop-and-wait loop. The DLQ is not wired through that path, so its SDK destination batching still withholds acks and is refused.  The v2 destination task writes a batch and then waits for every ack of it before the next read. With sdk.batch.size > 1 the SDK destination only enqueues on Write and acks when its batch flushes: when it reaches sdk.batch.size, or sdk.batch.delay after its first record. When a destination batch is larger than the records per write, acks are withheld, and with the default sdk.batch.delay of 0 nothing flushes by time, so the pipeline stops delivering while still reporting Running. With a delay it delivers, but one flush per write (one measurement: 83 rec/s against 56.7k rec/s on the default engine, with one-record reads and a 10ms delay). The classic engine reads acks on their own goroutine and is not affected.  The guard is conservative: any sdk.batch.size above 1 is refused, even where a particular write size would happen to align with the batch. Size 0 or 1, or sdk.batch.delay on its own, is safe (the SDK flushes synchronously at the size). Refusing turns a silent liveness failure into an actionable error. It fires before any connector is opened, so nothing is read and nothing is acked (invariants 1 and 3). Values that do not parse as an integer are left to the plugin's own config validation. The SDK trims keys and values before reading them, so the guard does too.  The error names every offending connector; ConfigPath and Fix address the first one, as a JSON pointer into the pipeline config document (/dead-letter-queue/settings/sdk.batch.size). Remove sdk.batch.size (and sdk.batch.delay) from the dead-letter queue, or run without --preview.pipeline-arch-v2 if the pipeline does not need record fan-out. See docs/operations/archv2-destination-batching.md.  A pipeline created through the API has no config document, so for it the error carries no ConfigPath and no Fix; the message still names the connector id and name and the setting. |
| `pipeline.config_changing` | Unavailable | CodePipelineConfigChanging is raised when a pipeline start is refused because an update, delete or connector/processor change on that pipeline is writing its config. Starting inside that window would build the run from a half-applied config, or for a pipeline that is being deleted. The change is a short store write, never a node operation. Unavailable: retry the start shortly. |
| `pipeline.config_persist_unknown` | Unavailable | CodeConfigPersistUnknown is raised when a pipeline create, update or delete could not be confirmed in the pipeline store: the write timed out, was retried once, and timed out again. The store may or may not hold the change, and until the next start this instance's view of the pipeline may differ from it; the next start loads what the store holds. Unavailable: check the database, then get the pipeline after the next start and repeat the change if it is missing. |
| `pipeline.dlq_not_recoverable` | FailedPrecondition | CodePipelineDLQNotRecoverable is raised when a pipeline's dead-letter queue cannot preserve the record content, so a record routed to it would be unrecoverable (invariant 3: at-least-once, no silent drop). Today that is the built-in log connector without payload:true when nacked records are routed to it (window-nack-threshold above 0, or window-size 0); it logs only hashes, so a nacked record's key and payload are lost. The default DLQ (window-size 1, threshold 0) routes no records and is not refused. The operator must configure a destination that stores the record, set payload:true on builtin:log explicitly, or set the nack threshold to 0 so a nack stops the pipeline instead. |
| `pipeline.duplicate_source_position` | FailedPrecondition | CodeDuplicateSourcePosition is returned when a single batch read from a source contains two or more records carrying identical position bytes, and that batch is fanned out to multiple destinations.  A position is a record's identity: multiAckNacker keys its per-position unanimity tally on it, and connector.Source.Ack advances the persisted position from it. Two records sharing one position make those two things ambiguous — the tally cannot tell the records apart, so one of them could never reach unanimity, and because positions are released to the source strictly in order (invariant 4), a single unresolvable slot silently stops the WHOLE batch from ever being acked. The pipeline would keep running, reading and writing records, while its source position never advanced and no error was ever surfaced.  Failing loudly here is deliberate. At-least-once is not violated by the stall (nothing is acked, so nothing is lost — the records replay on restart), but a silent, unbounded liveness failure is far worse for an operator than a clear error naming the offending connector behaviour. Emitting duplicate positions within one batch is a connector contract violation, so this is a user-actionable error, not an internal assertion. |
| `pipeline.empty_source_position` | FailedPrecondition | CodeEmptySourcePosition is returned when a batch about to be acked to the source contains a record with an empty/nil position.  connector.Source.Ack persists State.Position = p[len(p)-1] unconditionally, so acking an empty position OVERWRITES the durable source position with nothing: on restart the source resumes from an empty position — a full re-snapshot for Postgres, offset 0 for file/Kafka. That is an invariant-2 (monotonic, crash-safe positions) violation.  There are two distinct causes, and the suggestion names both because they call for different fixes.  The one reachable today is a SOURCE CONNECTOR emitting a record with an empty position, which is then acked or nacked. Nothing in the read path validates positions, so it reaches Worker.Ack/Worker.Nack unaltered. Like CodeDuplicateSourcePosition, that is a connector contract violation — every record must carry a distinct, non-empty position.  The second is a processor-chain shape: Batch.SplitRecord gives every piece after the first a nil position, so a sub-batch covering only the tail of a split run collapses to nils. On the ack path this is reachable; on the nack path the run ledger currently withholds split members and forwards the run's own non-nil origPos instead, so the guard there is a contract check rather than a live route. |
| `pipeline.fanout_requires_arch_v2` | FailedPrecondition | CodeFanOutRequiresArchV2 is raised when a processor returns a fan-out result (sdk.MultiRecord — one input record producing N output records, e.g. ai.chunk, split, clone) on the classic default pipeline engine, which is one-record-in-one-record-out and cannot run it. Record fan-out needs the preview engine, pipeline architecture v2 (pkg/lifecycle-poc/funnel), enabled with --preview.pipeline-arch-v2 or preview.pipeline-arch-v2: true; the postgres-pgvector-rag template is one such pipeline. A single pipeline engine that supports record fan-out is planned (design #2971). FailedPrecondition: the pipeline as configured cannot run on this engine. |
| `pipeline.instance_not_found` | NotFound | CodePipelineNotFound is raised when a referenced pipeline instance cannot be located. |
| `pipeline.name_already_exists` | AlreadyExists | CodePipelineNameAlreadyExists is raised when a pipeline config's name collides with an existing pipeline's name. |
| `pipeline.name_missing` | InvalidArgument | CodePipelineNameMissing is raised when a pipeline config is missing the required name field. |
| `pipeline.not_running` | FailedPrecondition | CodePipelineNotRunning is raised when an operation requires the pipeline to be running, but it is currently stopped. |
| `pipeline.retry_not_converging` | FailedPrecondition | CodeRetryNotConverging is returned when Worker.doTask's RecordFlagRetry self-recursion (see worker.go's retryAttempt) detects that a processor is not making progress on a retried sub-batch, or has exceeded the hard iteration cap that backstops that detection.  ProcessorTask.Do marks a sub-batch RecordFlagRetry for exactly those records the processor returned NO result for, then Worker.doTask re-feeds that sub-batch to the same task. If the same records come back unresolved again and again, the recursion is a fixpoint: it would recurse forever, growing the goroutine stack without bound until it hit Go's 1GB limit and crashed the ENTIRE process - not just the offending pipeline - with an unrecoverable fatal error. See #2726.  What actually triggers this, and what does NOT: a processor that simply returns FEWER records than it received is NOT this condition. ProcessorTask.Do rejects an empty result and pads exactly len(in)-len(out) entries, so such a processor shrinks the retry group every round and converges normally - a size threshold or a rate-limit path that returns partial results is fine. The reachable trigger is a record that comes back with no result AT ALL: for a standalone (WASM) processor, a ProcessedRecord whose Record oneof is unset, which in practice means a malformed or version-mismatched plugin.  This is fixed loudly instead of silently: nothing in the un-converged sub-batch (or anything after it in the same batch - Worker.doTask's tainted loop never advances its cursor past a Retry group it recursed into) is ever acked or nacked before this error is returned, so every record in it is redelivered on restart (invariant 3). No source position is corrupted or skipped (invariant 2). |
| `pipeline.running` | FailedPrecondition | CodePipelineRunning is raised when an operation requires the pipeline to be stopped, but it is currently running. |
| `pipeline.shared_destination_poisoned` | Aborted | CodeSharedDestinationPoisoned is returned when a worker in an N-source pipeline (slice 3b) tries to enter a shared destination subtree that a PREVIOUS pass already poisoned, after an error left the shared destination's single gRPC ack stream desynchronized. See Worker.doTask's poisoning store/check for the mechanics, and the adversarial-review finding this closes (H2, docs/design-documents/20260801-archv2-multiconnector-nsource.md).  This is a Tier-1 invariant-1 backstop, not merely retry hygiene. DestinationTask.Do writes a batch and reads back exactly that many acks off the destination's single gRPC stream, matching each ack to the position it just sent in strict send order; if Do returns early on an Ack() error, whatever acks were still queued behind it are never read by THIS pass. Without this check, the very next worker to acquire the shared boundary's mutex would read those leftover acks as if they were its own - and connector-defined positions are only unique WITHIN a source, so two sources emitting byte-identical position bytes (routine: two file sources, two offset-based connectors, ...) would make validateAcks' byte-for-byte comparison PASS, silently acking records upstream that this worker's own destination write never durably confirmed.  Recovering from this requires a full pipeline restart (a fresh Sink, a fresh gRPC stream, and therefore a fresh, unpoisoned TaskNode) - which is exactly what happens once this error propagates through Worker.Do/lifecycle-poc.Service.runPipeline's existing tomb-kill and recovery/degrade classification, so no special-casing is needed beyond returning this error from doTask. |
| `pipeline.shutting_down` | Unavailable | CodeShuttingDown is raised when a pipeline start is refused because Conduit has begun shutting down: once shutdown starts, no new pipeline run is started (including automatic recovery restarts), so that every run is drained before positions are flushed and the database is closed. Unavailable: retry against the instance after it restarts. |
| `pipeline.split_run_straddles_fanout` | FailedPrecondition | CodeSplitRunStraddlesFanOut is returned when a batch reaching a multi-destination fan-out holds only part of a split run — i.e. a processor before the fan-out split a record, and a later pre-fan-out processor resolved only some of the resulting pieces (for example by returning fewer records than it received, which marks the remainder Retry).  The run-completion ledger (see run_ledger.go) is per-Batch, and Batch.clone gives each branch its own copy so branches cannot race or bleed decisions into each other. That copy carries the run's whole-run member count, so a branch holding only part of the run can never complete it — and neither can the parent side. The run's original source position would then be withheld forever while later positions ack past it, silently skipping the record on restart.  Failing loud is deliberate and restores the behaviour that predates the ledger: this shape already failed loud before (via CodeEmptySourcePosition on the nil-position tail), and silently withholding would have disarmed that backstop. Nothing is acked and nothing is lost — the records are redelivered on restart (invariant 3). Joining a run's tally across fan-out branches is possible but is deliberately not attempted here without a real use case. |
| `pipeline.status_persist_failed` | Unavailable | CodeStatusPersistFailed is raised when a pipeline's status could not be written to the pipeline store. The in-memory status, which the API, the CLI and the lifecycle read, has already moved; the store still holds the previous status, which is what the next boot will act on. The lifecycle treats the write as a report: a run whose status was not persisted keeps running, and Start and Stop do not return this error. Check the database (/healthz, free disk) and whether position writes are failing too. Unavailable: the store may accept the write later. |
| `pipeline.stopping` | Unavailable | CodePipelineStopping is raised when a pipeline start is refused because the pipeline's previous run has stopped but is still writing its terminal status. Starting a new run in that window would let the old run's status overwrite the new run's. Unavailable: retry the start shortly. The window lasts until one status write returns, which is bounded (30s) on every database. |
| `pipelines.init_destination_exists` | AlreadyExists | CodeDestinationExists is raised by `pipelines init` when the resolved pipeline file already exists and --force was not passed. This is the fix for the command's previous behavior: os.OpenFile with O_TRUNC and no existence check, which silently overwrote an existing pipeline configuration. --force opts into the overwrite; --dry-run never touches the filesystem and is exempt from this check entirely (see InitCommand.checkDestination).  codes.AlreadyExists classifies to exitcode.Validation (2) via pkg/conduit/exitcode, the same bucket as pkg/scaffold's analogous CodeDestinationExists for connector/processor scaffolding. |
| `pipelines.init_path_unwritable` | FailedPrecondition | CodePipelinesPathUnwritable is raised by `pipelines init` when the *shape or accessibility of the destination path* prevents the write: something that is not a directory already occupies the path, a path component is unreadable or unwritable, the pipeline file path is itself a directory, or a parent directory does not exist (which is what a pipeline name containing a path separator produces). It is scoped by isDestinationShapedError in init.go — deliberately NOT every failure the create/open can return. A full device, a quota, or an I/O error is not a destination problem and stays on conduiterr.CodeInternal (exit 1), so that "disk full" cannot classify differently depending on whether the filesystem reports ENOSPC at open (macOS) or at write (Linux).  "The pipeline file already exists" is CodeDestinationExists, not this.  It replaces the generic conduiterr.CodeInternal ("internal.error", exit 1) this path used to return for everything. internal.error is the unclassified-bug bucket; an unwritable destination is an ordinary, user-fixable condition, and reporting it as a bug both misleads the user and makes the CLI's exit code useless for branching.  codes.FailedPrecondition classifies to exitcode.Validation (2), not Environment (3): in this codebase Environment means a dependency Conduit needs is unreachable (the server, the database, a bound listen address), whereas the destination path is part of the request itself — it comes from --pipelines.path (default ./pipelines) and the positional pipeline name. The remediation is always "point the command somewhere writable, or make this path writable", which is caller-side, so Validation is the honest bucket even when the underlying OS error is EACCES.  Known inconsistency, deliberately not resolved here: pkg/scaffold (`connectors new`) and cmd/conduit/root/initialize (`conduit init`) both map an equivalent MkdirAll failure on a user-supplied path to an Internal code and exit 1. Aligning all three is worth a follow-up; this command is the one a developer-experience audit found, and exit 2 is the correct answer for it. |
| `pipelines.init_template_flags_exclusive` | InvalidArgument | CodeTemplateFlagsExclusive is raised when --template (including the literal value "list") is combined with --source/--destination. A named template already fully determines the source+destination+settings triple; mixing it with --source/--destination is ambiguous by construction, so this is rejected rather than silently picking a winner (templates workstream doc §7). |
| `pipelines.init_template_version_mismatch` | FailedPrecondition | CodeTemplateVersionMismatch is raised when an embedded template's pinned connector settings no longer match the parameter shape of the built-in connector actually compiled into this binary. This is a packaging bug in the vendored template (the fixture drifted from the connector version this release ships), not a user config error — refusing up front here is strictly better than scaffolding a pipeline that parses fine but fails far away, and confusingly, at `conduit run` (templates workstream doc §7's "version-pinned mismatch" row). codes.FailedPrecondition classifies to exitcode.Validation (2). |
| `pipelines.init_unknown_template` | InvalidArgument | CodeUnknownTemplate is raised by `pipelines init --template <name>` when name doesn't match any entry in the embedded template gallery (see template_gallery.go). codes.InvalidArgument classifies to exitcode.Validation (2): the fix is on the caller's side (a typo, or a template that doesn't exist yet), not the environment. |
| `plugin.builtin_schema_unscoped` | Internal | CodeBuiltinSchemaUnscoped is raised when a built-in connector or processor calls the SDK schema service (schema.Get or schema.Create) with a context that was not derived from a call Conduit made into that plugin, so Conduit cannot tell which runtime's schema registry the call belongs to. The call is refused rather than answered from another runtime's registry. It indicates a bug in the plugin (for example a goroutine started with context.Background() that resolves schemas): pass the context Conduit hands to Open, Read, Write or Process down to schema calls. Internal: a plugin bug, not a configuration problem. |
| `plugin.standalone_env_passed` | FailedPrecondition | CodeEnvPassedToPlugins is the stable code carried by the startup log event and by the `plugins.standalone_env` doctor finding when the host environment contains variables that standalone connector plugin processes will inherit and whose names look like credentials or configuration secrets. It is registered in conduiterr so the code set that llms.txt publishes, and that alerting can rely on, stays complete. |

| `processor.egress_blocked` | PermissionDenied | CodeEgressBlocked is raised when a built-in processor (webhook.http, ollama.request, openai.*, cohere.*) is about to connect to an address that the dial-time guard refuses: a private, loopback, link-local, metadata, reserved or embedded-IPv4 address, whether given as an IP literal (in any encoding), reached through a DNS name, or reached through a redirect. The fix is for an operator to allow the specific host:port in processors.egress.builtin-allow and restart; it cannot be changed through the API. |
| `processor.instance_not_found` | NotFound | CodeProcessorNotFound is raised when a referenced processor instance cannot be located. |
| `processor.js_cyclic_output` | InvalidArgument | CodeJSCyclicOutput is raised when the record a script returns contains a map or slice that holds itself, directly or through other values (for example `record.Payload.After["self"] = record.Payload.After`). Such a record cannot be cloned, encoded or walked: every recursive consumer would overflow the stack, which is a fatal runtime error that takes down every pipeline in the process. The record is not emitted. It fails like any other processor error: with a DLQ enabled it is routed to the dead-letter queue, otherwise the pipeline degrades. The message names the path where the cycle closes. |
| `processor.js_output_limit_exceeded` | ResourceExhausted | CodeJSOutputLimitExceeded is raised when the record a script returns nests deeper than 10,000 levels, or expands to more than about 16.7 million map entries and slice elements once shared values are counted at each place they appear (a value referenced from many parents is copied once per parent by Record.Clone). Both would exhaust the stack or memory of the whole process in the next recursive consumer. The record is not emitted and nothing is truncated; it fails like any other processor error. ResourceExhausted: the output exceeds a fixed limit. |
| `processor.js_script_not_regular` | InvalidArgument | CodeJSScriptNotRegular is raised when script.path (or a required module) is not a regular file: a FIFO would block the read forever and a device never ends. |
| `processor.js_script_too_large` | ResourceExhausted | CodeJSScriptTooLarge is raised when script.path (or a required module) names a file larger than 10 MiB. The whole file would be read into memory and compiled, on every pipeline start, by a setting an API writer controls. Nothing is truncated; use a smaller script. |

| `provisioning.live_apply_unauthorized` | FailedPrecondition | CodeLiveApplyUnauthorized is raised by ApplyPlanLive when it refuses to apply a restart-class (EffectRestart) change to a currently-running pipeline because the caller did not authorize it — see ApplyPlanLive's allowRestartOnRunning parameter and docs/design-documents/20260708-live-server-deploy-apply.md, "Item 6 (reworked conservative): the data-path gate". | `provisioning.pipeline_id_duplicate` | InvalidArgument | CodePipelineIDDuplicate is raised when two pipeline documents — in the same file or across files — declare the same pipeline ID.  It is distinct from config.CodeIDDuplicate, which config.Validate raises for a connector/processor ID collision *within* a single pipeline document: that check has the whole document in hand. A pipeline-ID collision spans documents (and files), which config.Validate never sees (it validates one config.Pipeline at a time) — detecting it is the job of whatever collects pipelines across a directory: today that's Service.findDuplicateIDs (a bare sentinel, ErrDuplicatedPipelineID, since it only needs to skip the offending pipelines during provisioning) and the offline `conduit pipelines validate` engine (cmd/conduit/internal/validate, which needs a real code + configPath per finding for its report). |
